does: Copies the look of an eoc::character_creation::Appearance into the dummy's ecl::character_creation::TargetVisualComponent: the four colour ids from +0x58, +0x68, +0x78, +0x88 of the appearance into +0x40, +0x50, +0x60, +0x70 of the target, the visuals array from +0xA8 into +0x10, the elements from +0xB8 into +0x20 and the additional choices from +0xC8 into +0x30; before that it adds one to the int at +0x8 of the target unless the value at +0x0 is -1. It runs once each time the dummy definition's ChangeId2 moves.

evidence.says: the macOS build's symbol ecl::character_creation::SubsystemHelper::FillTargetVisualComponentColorsAndMaterials(TargetVisualComponent&, Appearance const&) at bg3_macos_x64+0x3A1EDD0 has the same body statement for statement: the same test of -1, the same increment and the same four 16-byte copies between the same offsets
two parameters are used, the target and the appearance; the offsets above

a count-only probe over nine seconds of a change-appearance session shows exactly one call, from inside the per-frame dummy update (bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x202F166), after one client write of ChangeId2 + 1 on the dummy definition
